thread:
Maria: Heads-up — gpunode-42 came back from the floor with intermittent Xid 31s during a customer run. Ops flagged it and we returned it to staging. I want to propose an extended burn-in workflow before we push it back.
Devin: Ugh Xid 31 again. Did ops capture dmesg + nvidia-smi logs?
Ops-bot: @Maria, logs uploaded: s3://redwood-ops/gpunode-42/1765001234/ (dmesg, nvidia-smi.txt, gpu_fans.csv) :white_check_mark:
Maria: yes, logs attached. dmesg shows repeated ECC single-bit corrections followed by a machine check and gpu reset. Not convincing it's thermal but not ruled out.
Kevin: Quick checklist: power cycle -> reseat -> run short stress -> re-run customer trace. Did we do power cycle?
Lee: We did reseat and power cycle on the rack this morning. Reseat didn't change behavior.
Sara: Suggest we escalate to extended soak + targeted mem tests. Short runs miss flaky cards. Proposal below.
Maria: Proposal: quarantine node + label it quarantined in k8s, run 48h extended burn with mixed workloads: gpu-burn (power/ALU), cuda-memtest (VRAM), tensorflow microbench (cache/SM stress), and random spike loads to reproduce ECC/Xid. If flake reproduces -> mark for RMA. If clean -> 24h soak in staging with sample customer traces. Thoughts?
Devin: Sounds good. Couple of tweaks: add a cyclic cold-start every 12h (simulate reboot during heavy load) and collect nvml counters periodically.
Kevin: Agreed. Also capture kernel oops + perf top during reproducer. If we see another Xid, capture full coredump and nv-hostengine logs.
Lee: Who runs it and where? We should avoid using production queues.
Maria: Run on staging cluster in us-west-2 on dedicated pool 'staging-burn' — ops reserved 4 cards for the next 72h. I'll own orchestration for the first 24h, Devin will own after.
Sara: Test harness (draft):
```bash
# quarantine node
kubectl label node gpunode-42 redwood/quarantine=true
# stress launcher (run inside node via debug pod)
./gpu-burn -t 3600 --mode all &
python cuda_memtest.py --duration 3600 &
stress-ng --gpu 0 --timeout 3600s
# collect nvml snapshots every 5m
while true; do nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv >> /tmp/gpu_snap.csv; sleep 300; done &
```
Devin: For kernel dumps use kdump + netconsole; ensure crashkernel reserved. Ops, can we enable kdump on that node image?
Ops-bot: kdump enabled on staging-burn image v2.3. Crashkernel set to 512M.
Kevin: Add stress patterns that hit ECC: prolonged small-allocation/free loops and concurrent multi-stream kernels. Those tend to trigger memory controller edge cases.
Maria: Good note. Also add a reproducible customer trace replay: we have the exact request sequence from the failing session — replay at 1x and 2x.
Sara: Logging checklist: nv-hostengine.log, nvidia-smi dmon, /var/log/kern.log, dmesg snapshot on Xid, coredumps, perf.data, and metrics posted to grafana for correlation.
Lee: Timeline: start tonight 22:00 UTC, run 48h. I'll be on rotation for first shift. Who's second?
Devin: I'll take the 22:00-04:00 UTC window. I'll add automated alert if Xid>=1 occurs via soak-bot.
Soak-bot: Alert rule created: notify #eng-infra if Xid >= 1 or ECC errors > 5 within 10m for node gpunode-42.
Maria: If we reproduce Xid within 48h -> lab RMA, don't put back in rotation. If clean -> 72h in staging soak with production traces then green.
Kevin: Do we want to try swapping to a different PCIe slot on that same board? If something's flaky at the slot level it's not the card. Possible but that's heavy.
Maria: Hold off swap for now unless we can't reproduce. We want to be conservative before opening device.
Sara: I'll prepare the post-run checklist and a short runbook for on-call: how to triage, where to find logs, RMA flow.
Maria: Thanks all — will kick off and post updates. :thumbsup:
Devin: Thanks — ping me if it trips, I'll grab coredump immediately.
Lee: On it.
Ops-bot: Burn started: gpunode-42, 1765001234 -> job id burn-1765001234, started 2026-03-18T22:00:00Z
Maria: Update 04:00 UTC — nvml counters show rising correctable ECCs, 2 Xid events captured during memory allocator loop, uploading snapshot now. If they trend up we'll start RMA prep.
Devin: Received snapshot, parsing now. If we see parity margins drop it's prob hardware.
Maria: End of thread for now — will file a follow-up postmortem if RMA performed.
